<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `84cf0fba0513ec4fc0a8e17a145be9a4ca05725e` — the merge of head `875682eeb8b5bf5c1021f9df6e83d173ae4162b5` into base `82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 84cf0fba0513ec4fc0a8e17a145be9a4ca05725e && git checkout 84cf0fba0513ec4fc0a8e17a145be9a4ca05725e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 875682eeb8b5bf5c1021f9df6e83d173ae4162b5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 && git merge --no-ff 875682eeb8b5bf5c1021f9df6e83d173ae4162b5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A4 · Fixes #32528 · declaration face (the claim on #32528 declared `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, and the diff adds an export to the package root).

### ① Derived judgments

- Matches the maintainer ruling on #32528 (comment 6879501332, option B): the engine refusal (`settleBulkStoredExpressions`) and ADR-0058 Addendum II D3 are untouched; the change is one authoring warning that prescribes `get_record` → `loop` → `update_record` by id.
- "Stored computed field" agrees with the engine's own test: `isStored` = not `formula` and declares `expression`, the same as `planStoredExpressions` (`packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`).
- "Input" agrees with the engine's reader: `bareFields` plus each traversal's first hop from `analyzeRelationshipTraversals`, the same set `storedExpressionReads` builds; following stored→stored reads matches `storedExpressionsReading`'s closure. A stored field set in the patch is not an input, which matches the engine replacing caller values for plan entries.
- `multi` is read with the executor's own `cfg.multi === true` (`crud-nodes.ts` `update_record`), and `fields` is the executor's one write-map key.
- Objects are read through `objectsAsServed`, so extension fields count; unknown targets, non-CEL dialects and unparseable sources are silent. Fine for an advisory.
- Severity is warning (no gate), reached through the existing `lintFlowPatterns` authoring rule; nothing that built, validated, saved or published before is refused.
- Tests pin the main shapes (direct input, transitive stored reader, reference hop, extension field, loop body, single-record silence, authoring-rule severity, `os explain`).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/lint` patch is right (no Metadata-protocol kind; a widening ships `patch`). The declaration line is not:

- **S1 (should-fix) — `Clause-②` declared `no`, should be `yes (widening)`.** The diff adds `FLOW_MULTI_UPDATE_MOVES_STORED_INPUT` to `packages/lint/src/index.ts` (the package's root export) and a new advisory on the authoring doors. That widens the public surface, which is what `yes (widening)` declares; the claim on #32528 already declared it, and the same shape was declared that way on #33321 ("two advisory rules and their exports are added"). The ruling changed *how* it widens (an advisory instead of per-row compute), not *whether*. "Nothing that passed before is refused" is the test for narrowing, not for widening. Fix: `Clause-②: yes (widening) — …` in the PR body and in `.changeset/32528-flow-multi-update-stored-input.md`; `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` stay.

### ③ Boundary flags

- None on security or data: read-only lint, no engine change.
- **N1 (nit)** `storedInputsByObject(stack)` parses every stored expression of every object on each `lintFlowPatterns` call, also on stacks with no `multi` update (the flow save/publish doors run it on the served snapshot). Building it lazily on the first `multi: true` update would cost nothing on the common path.
- **N2 (nit)** The prescribed shape caps the sweep at `get_record`'s `limit`, where the `multi` update had no such cap. "`limit` above 1" reads as "any number over 1"; the `os explain` paragraph could say "a `limit` that covers the rows the filter matches", so a sweep does not silently stop short.
